introduction: On this third Sunday of Lent, God speaks to Moses from the burning bush, reveals his name, and promises to free his people. In the Gospel, Jesus calls us to repent, and tells the parable of the fig tree that is given one more year to bear fruit. Paul warns us not to take God's gifts for granted. Let us turn to the patient and merciful God who gives us time to change.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and rich in love. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may call all people to conversion with the patience of the vinedresser. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the oppressed and enslaved: that God, who heard the cry of his people in Egypt, may set them free. Let us pray to the Lord.
For victims of violence, accidents and disasters, and for their families: that they may find comfort in God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who keep putting off their conversion: that they may hear the Lord's call today. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may use this Lent to bear fruit for God. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Merciful God, you heard the cry of your people and came down to save them. Give us the grace of true repentance, and make our lives bear fruit for you. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: One more year
reflection.body:
Moses is tending sheep in the desert when he sees a strange sight: a bush that burns but is not consumed. When he comes closer, God calls him by name and tells him to remove his sandals, "for the place you are standing on is holy ground." Then God reveals his heart: "I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry... I have come down to deliver them." God is not distant from suffering.

When Moses asks for his name, God answers, "I AM WHO I AM." This is the God who is always present, faithful from generation to generation.

In the Gospel, people tell Jesus about Galileans killed by Pilate while offering sacrifice. Jesus also mentions eighteen people killed when a tower fell in Siloam. Were they worse sinners than others? "I tell you, no," Jesus says. Disaster is not a punishment for being more sinful. But he adds a call to everyone: "unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way."

Then he tells a parable. A fig tree has produced no fruit for three years, and the owner wants it cut down. But the gardener pleads for it: "Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it and fertilize it." God is patient with us. He gives us time, and he works on us. But the time is not unlimited.

Paul reminds the Corinthians that the Israelites received great gifts in the desert, yet many fell away. "Therefore let him who thinks he stands be careful that he doesn't fall."

Lent is the gardener's extra year. What fruit is God waiting for in your life? This week, make a good confession, and let the Lord dig around the roots of your heart.
